rubrics.justification: Generally recognizes a good-quality blastocyst and appropriately notes limits of a single static image, but it questions the reported hatching status and gives somewhat equivocal ICM assessment despite the provided 4AA lab grade.
Integrates age, AMH/FSH, prior failed cycles, semen quality, endometrial thickness, BMI, and lifestyle with embryo quality well, though the discussion of the DOR label is somewhat overemphasized.

Reasoning is mostly logical and the implantation estimate is tied to embryo quality, age, and prior failures; minor inconsistency comes from simultaneously relying on and questioning the morphology grade.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice: favorable prognosis with single embryo transfer, caution about add-ons, and selective rather than routine PGT-A at age 34. Minor deviation is some uncertainty around Gardner stage interpretation.
Provides clear practical next steps for current transfer and future planning, including SET, luteal support, uterine cavity reassessment, embryology review, and when to consider PGT-A.
